blocks.en: Introduction: The Task Is Not Yet Done
blocks.es_reference: Introducción: La Tarea Aún No Está Terminada

blocks.en: We have come to the end of our study, but the task itself has not come to an end. For all that God has done across the centuries — for all the giants and the martyrs, the translations and the churches — the Great Commission is still unfinished. There remain whole peoples on the earth who have never once heard the name of Jesus. In this final unit we ask three plain questions: What is the task that remains? Why does it still wait, after all these centuries? And what part will we — and especially the church in Mexico and Latin America — take in finishing it?
blocks.es_reference: Hemos llegado al final de nuestro estudio, pero la tarea misma no ha llegado a su fin. A pesar de todo lo que Dios ha hecho a través de los siglos — a pesar de todos los gigantes y los mártires, las traducciones y las iglesias — la Gran Comisión todavía no está terminada. Quedan en la tierra pueblos enteros que nunca han oído ni una sola vez el nombre de Jesús. En esta unidad final hacemos tres preguntas sencillas: ¿Cuál es la tarea que queda? ¿Por qué todavía espera, después de todos estos siglos? ¿Y qué parte tomaremos nosotros — y especialmente la iglesia en México y América Latina — en terminarla?

blocks.en: I. The Task That Remains
blocks.es_reference: I. La Tarea Que Queda

blocks.en: When Jesus gave the Great Commission, He did not tell us simply to reach every country; He told us to make disciples of every nation — every ethnos, every people, tribe, and tongue. The goal is the very scene that the apostle John was shown in heaven: "a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne" (Revelation 7:9, NKJV). Today the gospel has reached most of the countries of the world, and that is a great mercy. Yet thousands of distinct people groups still remain what missionaries call "unreached" — peoples among whom there is still no church strong enough to carry the gospel to its own. Many of them are found in a great band across North Africa, the Middle East, and Asia that is sometimes called the "10/40 Window." Billions of people are alive today who have never yet heard the gospel clearly even once. The task is not finished.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Jesús dio la Gran Comisión, no nos dijo simplemente que alcanzáramos cada país; nos dijo que hiciéramos discípulos a cada nación — cada etnia, cada pueblo, tribu y lengua. La meta es la escena misma que le fue mostrada en el cielo al apóstol Juan: "una gran multitud, la cual ninguno podía contar, de todas naciones y tribus y pueblos y lenguas, que estaban delante del trono" (Apocalipsis 7:9, RVG). Hoy el evangelio ha llegado a la mayoría de los países del mundo, y eso es una gran misericordia. Sin embargo, miles de grupos de pueblos distintos siguen siendo lo que los misioneros llaman "no alcanzados" — pueblos entre los cuales todavía no hay una iglesia lo bastante fuerte para llevar el evangelio a los suyos. Muchos de ellos se encuentran en una gran franja a través del norte de África, el Medio Oriente y Asia que a veces se llama la "Ventana 10/40." Miles de millones de personas viven hoy que nunca han oído el evangelio con claridad ni una sola vez. La tarea no está terminada.

blocks.en: II. Why It Still Waits
blocks.es_reference: II. Por Qué Todavía Espera

blocks.en: Why, after twenty centuries, is the task still not done? It is not because God is unwilling, for He is "not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance" (2 Peter 3:9, NKJV). It is not because the gospel has lost any of its power. The task still waits, in large part, because the church has not yet fully obeyed. There are still far too few laborers for so great a harvest, too little prayer, too little sacrifice, and far too many believers who have never seriously asked what part of the work belongs to them. The very failure we saw in the first church at Jerusalem — content to keep the gospel close to home — still slows the advance today. The unfinished task is therefore a summons: a call to the church to finish what the Lord Himself began.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué, después de veinte siglos, la tarea todavía no está hecha? No es porque Dios no quiera, porque Él es "no queriendo que ninguno perezca, sino que todos vengan al arrepentimiento" (2 Pedro 3:9, RVG). No es porque el evangelio haya perdido nada de su poder. La tarea todavía espera, en gran parte, porque la iglesia aún no ha obedecido del todo. Todavía hay demasiado pocos obreros para una mies tan grande, demasiado poca oración, demasiado poco sacrificio, y demasiados creyentes que nunca han preguntado en serio qué parte de la obra les pertenece. La misma falla que vimos en la primera iglesia en Jerusalén — contenta con mantener el evangelio cerca de casa — todavía frena el avance hoy. La tarea inconclusa es, por tanto, un llamado: un llamado a la iglesia a terminar lo que el Señor mismo comenzó.

blocks.en: III. A New Day for the Sending Church
blocks.es_reference: III. Un Nuevo Día para la Iglesia Que Envía

blocks.en: For most of the modern missionary era, the missionaries went out from Europe and North America. But that day is changing before our eyes. In our own time God is raising up a great new missionary force from the very lands that once only received missionaries — from Africa, from Asia, and from Latin America. The church across the global South is no longer merely a mission field; it is fast becoming a mission force. A phrase has arisen to describe the new reality: the gospel now goes "from everywhere to everywhere" — from every continent, to every continent.
blocks.es_reference: Durante la mayor parte de la era misionera moderna, los misioneros salían de Europa y Norteamérica. Pero ese día está cambiando ante nuestros ojos. En nuestro propio tiempo Dios está levantando una gran nueva fuerza misionera de las mismas tierras que antes solo recibían misioneros — de África, de Asia, y de América Latina. La iglesia a lo largo del Sur global ya no es solamente un campo misionero; rápidamente se está convirtiendo en una fuerza misionera. Ha surgido una frase para describir la nueva realidad: el evangelio ahora va "de todas partes a todas partes" — de cada continente, a cada continente.

blocks.en: IV. The Part of the Mexican Church
blocks.es_reference: IV. La Parte de la Iglesia Mexicana

blocks.en: And here we must speak plainly and directly to you. The church in Mexico stands today in a remarkable position. You share a continent, and deep ties of history, language, and culture, with much of Latin America and beyond. You have access, in many cases, to peoples and places that missionaries from the north cannot easily enter. And God has given you a vigorous and growing church. The same God who sent a shoemaker out from England and a tentmaker out from Tarsus is calling pastors and ordinary believers out from Mexico to take their place in the great work — to reach the unreached both at home and abroad, to send and support those who go, and to raise up a new generation that will carry the gospel to the ends of the earth. The Mexican church is not standing at the edge of the missionary story. By the grace of God, it may stand very near its center in the days to come.
blocks.es_reference: Y aquí debemos hablarte clara y directamente. La iglesia en México está hoy en una posición notable. Comparten un continente, y profundos lazos de historia, idioma y cultura, con gran parte de América Latina y más allá. Tienen acceso, en muchos casos, a pueblos y lugares en los que los misioneros del norte no pueden entrar fácilmente. Y Dios les ha dado una iglesia vigorosa y creciente. El mismo Dios que envió a un zapatero desde Inglaterra y a un fabricante de tiendas desde Tarso está llamando a pastores y a creyentes comunes desde México a tomar su lugar en la gran obra — a alcanzar a los no alcanzados tanto en casa como en el extranjero, a enviar y sostener a los que van, y a levantar una nueva generación que lleve el evangelio hasta lo último de la tierra. La iglesia mexicana no está parada en el borde de la historia misionera. Por la gracia de Dios, puede estar muy cerca de su centro en los días por venir.

blocks.en: V. How the Task Will Be Finished
blocks.es_reference: V. Cómo Se Terminará la Tarea

blocks.en: How, then, shall the task be finished? In the same ways the Lord has always used. By praying the Lord of the harvest to thrust out laborers into His harvest. By going ourselves, wherever He sends us. By sending and faithfully supporting those whom He calls to go. By giving, so that the work does not stall for lack of means. And by raising children and training leaders for the next generation — which is the very reason this seminary exists. No single one of us can finish the task alone. But every one of us can take our place; and together, under God, the work will be done. For the Lord Himself has promised: "this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come" (Matthew 24:14, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo, entonces, se terminará la tarea? De las mismas maneras que el Señor siempre ha usado. Rogando al Señor de la mies que envíe obreros a su mies. Yendo nosotros mismos, dondequiera que Él nos envíe. Enviando y sosteniendo fielmente a los que Él llama a ir. Dando, para que la obra no se detenga por falta de medios. Y criando hijos y entrenando líderes para la siguiente generación — que es la razón misma por la que existe este seminario. Ninguno de nosotros por sí solo puede terminar la tarea. Pero cada uno de nosotros puede tomar su lugar; y juntos, bajo Dios, la obra será hecha. Porque el Señor mismo ha prometido: "Y será predicado este evangelio del reino en todo el mundo, para testimonio a todas las naciones; y entonces vendrá el fin" (Mateo 24:14, RVG).

blocks.en: Conclusion: To the End of the Age
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión: Hasta el Fin del Mundo

blocks.en: We began this course with the God who sends, and we end it with the task He has given us to finish. The same story that ran from Abraham to Antioch, from Carey to the martyrs in the jungle, now runs through us. The fields are still white for harvest. The Lord of the harvest is still calling. And the last word of the Great Commission still stands as true today as it did on the mountain in Galilee: "lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age" (Matthew 28:20, NKJV). So go — or send, or pray, or give — but do not stand idle while the task remains unfinished. To Him who sends us, and who goes with us to the very end, be glory among all the nations.
blocks.es_reference: Comenzamos este curso con el Dios que envía, y lo terminamos con la tarea que Él nos ha dado por terminar. La misma historia que corrió desde Abraham hasta Antioquía, desde Carey hasta los mártires en la selva, ahora corre a través de nosotros. Los campos todavía están blancos para la siega. El Señor de la mies todavía está llamando. Y la última palabra de la Gran Comisión permanece tan verdadera hoy como en el monte de Galilea: "he aquí, yo estoy con vosotros todos los días, hasta el fin del mundo" (Mateo 28:20, RVG). Así que ve — o envía, u ora, o da — pero no te quedes ocioso mientras la tarea permanece inconclusa. A Aquel que nos envía, y que va con nosotros hasta el mismo fin, sea la gloria entre todas las naciones.

sa.prompt: What does the lesson mean when it says the Great Commission is still 'unfinished'?
sa.model: The lesson means that despite twenty centuries of gospel advance, there remain whole peoples on earth who have never once heard the name of Jesus. The Great Commission is 'unfinished' because thousands of distinct people groups are still unreached, with no church strong enough among them to carry the gospel to its own people.

sa.prompt: Explain the difference between reaching every country and reaching every 'ethnos' (people group). Use Revelation 7:9.
sa.model: Reaching every country is a matter of political borders, but reaching every 'ethnos' means reaching every distinct people group, tribe, and tongue — many countries contain dozens or hundreds of such groups, some reached and some not. Revelation 7:9 pictures the final goal as a great multitude of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues before the throne, showing the goal is ethnic and linguistic completeness, not merely national coverage.

sa.prompt: What is an 'unreached people group,' and where are many of them found?
sa.model: An 'unreached people group' is a people among whom there is still no church strong enough to carry the gospel to its own members without outside help. Many unreached peoples are found in a band across North Africa, the Middle East, and Asia sometimes called the '10/40 Window,' where billions of people are alive today who have never yet clearly heard the gospel even once.

sa.prompt: Why does the lesson say the task still waits after twenty centuries?
sa.model: The task still waits after twenty centuries not because God is unwilling, since He desires that all should come to repentance, and not because the gospel has lost power, but because the church has not yet fully obeyed. There are still too few laborers, too little prayer, too little sacrifice, and too many believers who have never seriously asked what part of the work belongs to them — the same failure of the Jerusalem church that stayed home still slows the advance today.

sa.prompt: How is the sending of missionaries changing in our own day?
sa.model: For most of the modern missionary era, missionaries went out from Europe and North America, but that is changing before our eyes. God is now raising up a great new missionary force from lands that once only received missionaries — Africa, Asia, and Latin America — so that the gospel now moves 'from everywhere to everywhere' rather than in one direction only.

sa.prompt: Why does the lesson say the church in Latin America is becoming a mission force, not only a mission field?
sa.model: The lesson says the church in Latin America is becoming a mission force, not only a mission field, because the church across the global South has grown vigorous and is now sending out its own missionaries rather than only receiving them. What was once purely a receiving region is now actively contributing laborers to reach the unreached elsewhere in the world.

sa.prompt: What remarkable position does the Mexican church hold, according to this unit?
sa.model: The Mexican church holds a remarkable position because it shares a continent, and deep ties of history, language, and culture, with much of Latin America and beyond, giving it access to peoples and places northern missionaries cannot easily enter. Combined with a vigorous and growing church, this means Mexico is positioned not at the edge of the missionary story but potentially very near its center in the days to come.

sa.prompt: List the ways the lesson says the task will be finished.
sa.model: The lesson says the task will be finished by praying the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers; by going ourselves wherever He sends us; by sending and faithfully supporting those He calls to go; by giving so the work does not stall for lack of means; and by raising children and training leaders for the next generation.

sa.prompt: How does Matthew 24:14 give hope and motivation for the unfinished task?
sa.model: Matthew 24:14 promises that 'this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.' This gives hope because it guarantees the task will ultimately be completed — God's purpose cannot fail — and it gives motivation because our faithful participation in preaching the gospel is tied directly to the fulfillment of that promise and the coming of Christ.

sa.prompt: Now that you have finished this course, what part will you take in the unfinished task? Be specific and prayerful.
sa.model: This is a personal, prayerful reflection question inviting the student, at the close of the course, to name a specific and honest commitment to go, send, pray, give, or train others for the unfinished task. A thoughtful answer avoids vague generalities and instead commits to something concrete the student can actually begin doing.
